answer: Honest agents trade widely, their transaction graph spreading like a lantern glow. A Sybil farm forms a closed spiral, tokens circling its own identities with few outside links — its graph mirrors a fraud ring, not a market. The network scores each identity by its economic openness: distinct established counterparties and outward value flow. Closed-loop identities pay higher fees and wait longer for rewards until they build real external ties. One honest-looking identity is cheap; a thousand that all look open requires bribing real counterparties, costing more than the rewards.
